Mr Kofi Amankwa-Manu (NPP — Atwima Kwanwoma): Mr Speaker, thank you for the opportunity to comment on the Budget as presented by His Excellency the President through the Minister for Finance to this House. Mr Speaker, in commenting on the Budget, I rely on two materials: the Message on the State of the Nation as presented by His Excellency to this House on Thursday, 27th February, 2025, and the Budget as presented by the Minister for Finance on 11th March, 2025. Mr Speaker, we are here talking about a man who is so unique in the politics of our nation, and I mean His Excellency President Mahama. This is somebody who has been a Vice President, a President, and has come again as President. Mr Speaker, having occupied all these positions, the President, His 165 20th March, 2025 166 Environmental Protection (Mining in Forest Reserves) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025 Excellency John Dramani Mahama, does not have the luxury of excuse. Mr Speaker, I have looked at the Budget, and this is a Budget I term the “Kwashiorkor Budget”. Mr Speaker, kwashiorkor in the sense that we were promised of a lean government. Yes, His Excellency has succeeded in reducing the number of Ministers, but the question I ask is, has he succeeded in saving the public purse? Mr Speaker, the answer is simply no. If we look at the amount of money going to government machinery, this is not an indication of a government that is prepared to save the public purse, and that is my definition of kwashiorkor Budget. Yes, the top is slim, but the stomach, where the chop-chop is going to be, is big, and anybody suffering from that kind

will bite all of us. In fact, if we do not deal with it now, it would affect the economy in general. So, I believe that the Minister must be encouraged to walk the talk. All of us should get on board, so that the situation does not get out of hand to necessitate another levy being introduced. Mr Speaker, that is all I have on this rising. Thank you so much. Mr First Deputy Speaker: Yes, Majority Leader and Chairman of the Business Committee? 3.00 p.m. Mr Ayariga: Mr Speaker, I think the Minister for Energy and Green Transition will, in due course, make the relevant policy pronouncements in this House. Indeed, there is a comprehensive plan by His Excellency, President John Dramani Mahama to deal with our energy challenge. The Minister has given several indications—[Interruption]—Mr Speaker, he asked the questions and asked us to raise the issues. Now that we are addressing the issues, he is behaving as if we are not responding to his issues. He asked questions and then we are trying to address his questions. Yes, Mr Speaker, I said the Minister for Energy and Green Transition will, in due course, be here, but several of the policies have already been put out there. One of them, of course, and I think he has mentioned it in this House, is the effort to move towards the use of gas instead of diesel to power our plants. The idea is that gas is far cheaper, so we are going to construct a second gas plant, which will, I believe, double our gas processing capacity in the country. If we use gas, we will be able to significantly drive down the cost of electricity in the country. On the issue of efficiencies, the Minister has already said in this House that the distribution sector would be privatised, so private sector participation in the distribution sector would take place. As we speak, some studies are ongoing, supported by our development partners, so that we can have transaction advisors, zone the country, and give out the various zones, so that the power generators will sell in bulk to a zone administrator who will then further distribute it, recover the cost and pay back. We believe that if that is done, the private sector will be able to ensure efficiency, deal with the issue of theft, as the Hon Member is complaining about, and then also recover the cost and pay back to the generators. So that Government is not burdened with the debts that accumulate because generators of power are not paid their money. On 43 13th June, 2025 44 Business of the House the issue of Monkeypox, I do agree with you that there may be a need for the Minister at a certain point to come to the House and brief us on the situation and what efforts are being put in place to contain any potential outbreak of the Monkeypox in the country. Mr Speaker, on the issues that the Minority Leader has raised, I am sure that the Minister for Finance will make himself available when it is appropriate to respond to any issues that we may put in a Question for him to respond to. If he feels that a matter of Government policy needs to be communicated to this House, he will come. As for the Energy Sector Levy (Amendment) Bill that was passed, if you recall, the argument that was used to back the levy was that it will be enforced to the extent that it will not lead to an increase in the ex-pump price of petroleum products. That was the condition under which this Side of the House accepted the levy. If implementing the levy will lead to an increase in the price of petroleum products, we will not allow that. Mr Speaker, by that time, petroleum prices were coming down and Government thought to harvest some of the benefits in order to deal with the energy sector financing challenges. When global circumstances change the environment of the pricing of petroleum products and the implementation of the levy will lead to an increase in the price, that goes against the arguments that informed the passage of the Bill. This is a Side that keeps its promise, the promise not to do anything that will increase the price of petroleum products in implementing the levy and cause an increase in the price of petroleum products. It was on that basis we halted it and when circumstances change and there is the possibility of harvesting the benefits for Ghanaians to solve the energy sector problem, we can go back to it. So, this is a Government that keeps its promises, and we promised not to increase prices, so we will do whatever it takes to keep 53 20th June, 2025 54 Business of the House prices as low as possible. Mr Speaker, if there is anything that needs to be done, maybe, just tinker with the transitional provisions of the Act. I think we have answered all the questions.
